title: health-food
text: This project investigates physical measurements and health metrics from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), provided by the primer.data R package.

title: health-food
section: Food Consumption Trends: Ultra-Processed vs. Minimally Processed Foods
text:
Food Consumption Trends: Ultra-Processed vs. Minimally Processed Foods
This graph tracks the proportion of daily calories coming from ultra-processed foods (shown in red) compared to whole and minimally processed foods (shown in green) among US adults over time.










Opposing Trends: As ultra-processed foods rose from 52.5% in 1999–2000 to over 57% by 2018–2020, whole and minimally processed foods fell from 33.5% to 27.4%.
Recent Shift: In the August 2021–August 2023 survey cycle, ultra-processed food intake dropped to 53.0%, while whole and minimally processed calories rose back to approximately 30.5%.

title: NHANES Health Insights
text: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) assesses the health and nutritional status of adults and children across the United States.

title: NHANES Health Insights
text:
Obesity Rates Over Time
Beyond individual age trajectories, national health surveys track how adult obesity prevalence has shifted across recent decades.










Rising Trend: Between 1999–2000 and 2017–2018, the US adult obesity rate increased from 30.5% to over 42%.
Recent Leveling: Rates remained above 41% entering 2020, and the August 2021–August 2023 survey recorded 40.3%, pointing to a recent stabilization.
